news.title: This is all kind of magical, and unfortunately some deep learning researchers understand i…
news.author: ngaylinn@tech.lgbt
news.snippet: This is all kind of magical, and unfortunately some deep learning researchers understand it that way. Often the word "embedding" means: I turned a thing into a vector that somehow captures everything that matters about the thing. There's a big problem with that: the latent embedding trick is about dimension reduction . It takes a very high-dimensional object and throws away information until you're left with just the details "that matter." The key question is: for what ? The answer is "whatever loss function you choose." An embedding vector isn't some objective, general purpose summary, because such a thing is not possible. You have to think about the loss function and how that affects the embedding space--then you have to report that along with your results ! I've been very frustrated lately by people hand waving over that step. Sometimes it's obvious and fine, but sometimes it's not, and regardless it's important to be precise. (2/2) # deeplearning # machinelearning

news.title: "Latent embedding" is an important concept in deep learning, and one that's often misunder…
news.author: ngaylinn@tech.lgbt
news.snippet: "Latent embedding" is an important concept in deep learning, and one that's often misunderstood. The basic idea is that by training a neural network with a "bottle neck" architecture, you can turn any collection of objects into an abstract space that represents the relationships between those objects. Any object in that set can be represented as a point within that space. Nearby points represent similar objects, and each direction within that space represents some meaningful kind of variation among those objects. This is really useful, since you can turn any object into a vector, and you can do useful things with those vectors like manipulate them with math or pass them into a neural network. You can also turn any vector in that space into a corresponding object, perhaps even a new object that makes sense in relation to the others, but hasn't been seen before! (1/2) # deeplearning # machinelearning
